Ben Mendoza

Independent candidate for U.S. Representative, District 23, Bexar County, Texas · Open seat

Mediator

Ben Mendoza is an El Paso native and professional mediator running as an independent for Texas's 23rd Congressional District. The Texas Secretary of State lists him as an independent candidate in the November 3, 2026 general election. The seat is open after former U.S. Rep. Tony Gonzales resigned earlier in 2026.

Where Mendoza stands

Border security
Supports federally funded full academy and supervised field training for ICE deportation officers. Proposes working with Mexico to protect both countries' borders.
Border wall in Big Bend
Opposes building a border wall in Big Bend.
Data centers
Says local communities should guide decisions on data centers, and that their representatives should guard against data centers using too much electricity and water.
School safety
Supports federal help with officer training and stronger security in school districts. Says local authorities should lead policing and protection.
Water
Calls for working with New Mexico to release more water from Elephant Butte, and for fair water sharing under international rules. Proposes working with the Army Corps of Engineers on flooding and conservation, including in Uvalde.
Energy costs
Proposes promoting and funding electric cooperatives to lower power costs.
Executive power
Says Congress needs to assert a check on the executive branch, as the Constitution provides, on national security matters.

Background

  • Occupation: mediator (Texas Secretary of State filing)
  • Education: B.A. in criminal justice, University of Texas at El Paso
  • Former regional director, education division, Newsweek Inc.; former district director, Time Inc.
  • Former sole proprietor, Al's Formal-Wear; former district executive, Yucca Council, Boy Scouts of America
  • Previous campaigns: U.S. House TX-16 (2018), El Paso City Council (2023 special election), El Paso mayor (2024), El Paso ISD board; has not held elected office
